arguments.value: 35-year-old pregnant woman at 11 weeks’ gestation evaluated for bilateral ovarian masses and a large presacral retroperitoneal mass after a history of severe leg pain. Imaging showed bilateral multilocular solid adnexal tumors and a ~10–12 cm sacral/spinal canal–extending mass; tumor markers were notable for elevated CA 19-9 with normal CA-125/CA15-3. She underwent surgery at 12 weeks with left salpingo-oophorectomy, right cystectomy, omental biopsy, and biopsy of the presacral lesion. Pathology revealed bilateral borderline seromucinous ovarian tumors and a presacral schwannoma, with no omental atypia. Pregnancy continued to term with planned C-section at 37 weeks due to obstruction from the presacral mass, and postpartum MRI showed stable schwannoma followed by definitive neurosurgical resection confirming WHO grade I schwannoma.
